units: <cite ref="Mishnah Sanhedrin 3:5">Snh. III, 5</cite> <he>האוהב והש׳</he> a friend and an enemy (are disqualified as witness or judge); <he>ש׳ כל שלא דבר וכ׳</he> an enemy is he who has not spoken to the person concerned for the last three days on account of his hostility.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 32b:16">B. Mets. 32ᵇ</cite> <he>אוהב לפרוק וש׳ לטעון מצוה בש׳ וכ׳</he> if there is a friend that needs help to unload, and an enemy that needs help to load, it is proper to help the enemy in order to bend his animosity.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 32b:18">Ib.</cite> <he>ש׳ דקרא</he> the case of the enemy mentioned in the Scripture (<cite ref="Exodus 23:5">Ex. XXIII, 5</cite>, where the release of the beast is concerned), <he>ש׳ דמתניתן</he> that of our Boraitha (just quoted).

<cite ref="Avot D'Rabbi Natan 23:1">Ab. d’R. N. ch. XXIII</cite> <he>מי שעושה שׁוֹנְאוֹ אוהבו</he> ed. Schechter (a hero is he) who makes his enemey to be his friend; a. e.—Pl. <he>שׂוֹנְאִים</he>, <he>שׂוֹנְאִין</he>.
<cite ref="Sotah 9a:13">Sot. 9ᵃ</cite> <he>משה ודוד שלא שלטו שׂוֹנְאֵיהֶם וכ׳</he> Moses and David over whose works their enemies got no control; a. fr.—
Succ. 29ᵃ, a. fr. שונאיהם של ישראל euphem. for Israel
